title: FP-MCP-233 Guarded Start Integrity Review
summary: Record an integrity review of the first successful guarded OpenCode execution path from FP-MCP-233. The engineering result remains real: popup-mediated local clearance was created, the remote runner accepted the guarded start, OpenCode started, and DESIGN_ONLY outputs were produced and committed. The governance and lifecycle result is not clean: popup-mediated clearance was used before FP-MCP-217 reconciliation was recorded, full FP-027 canary discipline evidence was not captured for the actual first start, approval consumption failed after start due the hardcoded FP-MCP-036 scope bug, and a bounded approval reuse window existed until the approval and local clearance expired. This packet records the historical truth without erasing the successful run or laundering the integrity gaps.
caveats: FP-MCP-233 was technically successful but governance-incomplete at the moment it ran.
Popup-mediated clearance was later adopted explicitly by FP-MCP-236, but that decision came after the FP-MCP-233 start and therefore does not retroactively make the original start clean.

The evidence does not prove process-tree snapshot immediately before runner contact, live abort-readiness check immediately before contact, or a formal no-retry/no-chaining state-machine gate for the actual first real start.
Approval consumption was not recorded after the successful start; the single-use guarantee did not mechanically close immediately after execution.
The approval and clearance reuse risk was bounded by expiry and by the requirement for another popup/tool call, but bounded risk is not the same as a fulfilled guarantee.
No evidence indicates that a second start was attempted with the same approval.
This packet is historical review only; it does not attempt retroactive consumption or any new start.
